topIssues.title: op-supernode: An older verified result can keep a stale L1 inclusion after an L1 reorg
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:**

## Summary

An older `VerifiedResult` can keep an `L1Inclusion` on an orphaned L1 fork after an L1 reorg. `superroot_atTimestamp` then returns a wrong `verified_required_l1` for that timestamp. `VerifiedBlockAtL1` also uses the stale value for finality.

The case is extremely unlikely. It needs all of these:

- An L1 reorg deeper than the virtual nodes' L1 follow distance. The virtual nodes derive only from L1 blocks at least that deep, so a shallower reorg cannot change a stored `L1Inclusion`. No L1 reorg on mainnet since the move to proof of stake has been this deep.
- The reorg moves a batch to a different L1 block number, but the L2 blocks stay the same. A batch that stays at the same number on the new fork leaves only a stale hash. That case does no harm, because the challenger and `VerifiedBlockAtL1` compare only the number.
- Within one interop round, the verifier's two L1 lookups see different forks. This needs an L1 RPC that answers from more than one view, for example backends at different heads behind a load balancer. With one consistent L1 node, it needs L1 to switch forks back and forth between two lookups that are milliseconds apart.

The gap is still in the consistency model, so this issue records it.

## How it happens

`observeRound` (`op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/interop.go`) checks for L1 reorgs in two steps:

1. It checks that the newest accepted result's `L1Inclusion` is canonical, by number.
2. Later, it checks that each chain's frontier L1 head is canonical, by number.

The rewind logic checks only the newest result. This is correct only if all accepted results are on one L1 fork. Each by-number lookup is a separate RPC call, and the L1 source's canonical view can change between two calls. Example:

1. On fork A, the batch for T-1 is at L1 block 100. The newest accepted result is T-1, with `L1Inclusion` A@100.
2. L1 reorgs to fork B. On fork B, the same batch is at block 102. The L2 block at T-1 does not change.
3. Step 1 runs while the L1 source still serves fork A. A@100 is canonical, so the verifier does not rewind.
4. The L1 source changes to fork B. The virtual nodes have already derived T on fork B, with L1 origin B@103.
5. Step 2 passes. Result T commits with `L1Inclusion` B@103.
6. Later rounds check only T. Nothing reads T-1 again, so T-1 keeps A@100.

The virtual node's safe head DB now records B@102 for T-1. `Interop.Reset` is a no-op, so the re-derivation does not update the verified DB.

## Impact

- `superroot_atTimestamp` returns `verified_required_l1` A@100 for T-1. The challenger compares only its number with the game's L1 head. For a game with L1 head 101, the challenger treats T-1 as derivable, but on the canonical chain T-1 needs block 102. The challenger can then take the wrong position and lose bonds.
- `VerifiedBlockAtL1` compares the stored `L1Inclusion` by number. It can report T-1 as finalized when L1 finality reaches 100, before the data at 102 is final.

## Options considered

Each option below has a gap or a cost. The right fix needs a decision about which database owns the L1 data and when a rewind is allowed.

- **Walk L1 by parent hash at commit.** Check that each frontier L1 head and the previous `L1Inclusion` are ancestors of the highest frontier head. This does not depend on the L1 source's view. Batches can be up to 12 hours apart on L1, so the walk can need thousands of sequential header fetches in one round.
- **One batch RPC for all canonical checks.** Check the previous `L1Inclusion` and all frontier heads in one batch. This lowers the risk a lot. Nodes do not guarantee that a batch is atomic, so the gap stays open.
- **Compute the required L1 block on read, from the safe head DB.** This builds one response from two databases that update at different times. A response can then pair `VerifiedRequiredL1` above `CurrentL1`. A verified timestamp can also go back to "not verified" while a node re-derives.
- **Confirm the newest result against the virtual nodes in the same round.** After the frontier read at T, read `OptimisticAt(T-1)` for each chain. Compare it with the stored L2 heads and `L1Inclusion`, and rewind on a mismatch. This finds the reorg through the nodes' own hash-linked derivation. It still depends on the frontier L1 heads of different chains being on one fork. Today separate L1 lookups check that.

The lokahi proof of concept (ethereum-optimism/optimism#24424) copies the same newest-result check, so it has the same gap.

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestSingleChainSuperFaultProofsFromL2CL/ClaimDirectToNextTimestamp-challenger`
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Tracking a flaky acceptance test failure.

**CI run:** https://app.circleci.com/jobs/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5977038
**Date:** 2026-11-26
**Job:** `memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` (parallel node 1, merge queue for #24319, contracts-only change)
**Observed duration:** subtest 5.53s, parent 55.62s
**CircleCI Insights:** not present in the current flaky-tests snapshot

```text
=== FAIL: op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/super-opnode TestSingleChainSuperFaultProofsFromL2CL/ClaimDirectToNextTimestamp-challenger (5.53s)
    Error Trace: op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go:360
                 op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/proof_runner.go:123
    Error:       Received unexpected error:
                 Post "http://127.0.0.1:42599": EOF
```

Package: `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/super-opnode`

`127.0.0.1:42599` is the devstack `tcpproxy` in front of the kona-node sequencer RPC (upstream `127.0.0.1:34029`). The failing call is `traceProvider.AbsolutePreState`. kona-node logged no error or restart during the subtest, and the system teardown only began ~0.4s after the subtest ended, so the connection was closed with no response while the node was healthy. Suspected (unverified): keep-alive race where the server closes an idle pooled connection as the client reuses it; Go does not retry a non-idempotent POST.

Related (closed): #21952 (`TestSingleChainSuperFaultProofsFromOpNode`, different symptom).

topPRs.title: rust: update reth to v2.8.1
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
> **Draft: reth is pinned by `rev`.** This pins `rev = fc4e457…` on the unmerged fork PR ethereum-optimism/reth#56, so the required `rust-reth-tag-pin` check stays red. Once #56 rebase-merges and `op-v2.8.1-0` is tagged, this PR repins to the tag and refreshes both lockfiles. Before it leaves draft, `op-v2.7.0` and `develop`'s pin get re-checked for new commits.

Tracking: ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#733.

## What

This moves the reth pin from `op-v2.7.0-2` to the new fork branch `op-v2.8.1`, on upstream [v2.8.1](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/releases/tag/v2.8.1). That is the last reth release before upstream replaced revm with evm2, so op-reth stays on revm 43 and alloy-evm 0.39. The evm2 migration is separate work (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#332).

**Fork patches:**
- The fork drops from 28 carried patches on v2.7.0 to 15 on v2.8.1. `rust/RETH-CARRIED-PATCHES.md` lists them.
- Two upstream fixes are new picks: paradigmxyz/reth#28598 and #28249.
- One fork-only test is new.

**Upstream fixes this brings in, which `develop` lacks**, include:
- paradigmxyz/reth#27586: `--rpc.gascap` for calls without a `gas` field. Closes the bug in ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#463.
- paradigmxyz/reth#27869: foreign-chain EIP-7702 authorizations. ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#470.
- paradigmxyz/reth#27864 and #27866: IPC request buffering. ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#472.

## Changes

**Pin and dependencies:**
- The 73 reth crates are on the fork's `rev`.
- reth's shared pins are synced: reth-core crates to 0.8.2, `revm-inspectors` to 0.44.3, `alloy-trie` to 0.9.8 and `alloy-hardforks` to 0.4.11.
- Both lockfiles lock `alloy-trie` at 0.9.8, because 0.9.9 breaks reth v2.8.1's `HashBuilder` literal.

**API adaptations:**
- **`reth-optimism-trie`**, for paradigmxyz/reth#27945:
  - the removed proof and witness builders,
  - `StateProofProvider::multiproof_v2` now taking `(targets, requires_masks)`,
  - `Proof::multiproof_v2` moving to `MultiProofCalculator`.

  Results are unchanged.
- **The vendored RPC memory overlay** returns `UnsupportedProvider` from `multiproof_v2`. That path is reachable only through `eth_getMultiProof`, which OP doesn't serve.
- **`ComputedTrieData` → `SortedTrieData`.**
- **`transaction_by_hash`** recovers senders through upstream's `recover_mined_transaction` (paradigmxyz/reth#27816).
- **The pool validator** seeds its own block gas limit from the latest header, so op-reth's redundant override is gone.

**Upstream changes op-reth now handles:**
- **Denied new flags**, each with a test that was red before the deny:
  - `--snap.v2`: snap/2 relies on block access lists.
  - `--cpu-cores`: op-reth doesn't size its runtime from it yet; follow-up in ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#734.
  - `--engine.prewarm-reuse`: OP execution can't reuse prewarm results, so `OpEvmConfig` keeps upstream's new hook disabled.
  - `--debug.lazy-kzg-settings`: op-reth's pool never loads KZG settings.
- **Pre-Canyon body withdrawals** are now rejected in `validate_block_pre_execution`, matching upstream's new pre-Shanghai check (paradigmxyz/reth#27715).
- **A provider failure computing the Isthmus withdrawals root** is now a processing error, not a consensus error, so a transient storage failure no longer marks a valid payload `INVALID`. Instead, `newPayload` returns an error that op-node retries.
- **Upstream mirrors:**
  - All 30 stale `UPSTREAM-MIRROR` tags were re-verified against the new pin and advanced.
  - The only code change from that re-verification is `transaction_by_hash`, above.
  - `validate_block_pre_execution` gets a new mirror tag.
- **Docs:** `RETH-CARRIED-PATCHES.md` is updated for `op-v2.8.1`. `UPDATING-RETH.md` gains notes on lockfile drift past reth's pins, LLVM 22 for checking the fork, and re-deriving reused sweep verdicts whose premise depends on the old base.

## Review

The `reth-update-reviewer` swept all 325 upstream commits in `v2.7.0..v2.8.1` with 6 partition agents, plus the forward sweep to upstream `main` at `7540d1dd1`.

**HIGH: paradigmxyz/reth#28249.** The forward sweep had rated it unreachable. Since paradigmxyz/reth#27651, the overlay behind op-reth's Isthmus withdrawals root uses the prefix-set path, which #28249 fixes.
- **Symptom upstream:** a v2 proof-calculator panic in the invalid-block witness hook, which is on by default in op-reth.
- **Storage roots:** targeted and randomised tests found them unaffected.
- **Resolution:** picked in #56, with a structural test that is red without the fix and green with it.

**Other findings, all resolved here:** the flag denials, pre-Canyon withdrawals, the withdrawals-root error mapping, and the `transaction_by_hash` mirror.

A second review covered everything added after the first, including the denials, the pre-Canyon check, the error mapping, the gas-limit cleanup, `transaction_by_hash` and the #28249 pick. It was clean apart from nits. It confirmed:
- No legitimate pre-Canyon body carries `Some` withdrawals. op-reth stores and serves `None`, and the pipeline re-requests from another peer if one does.
- The sender cache can't return a wrong sender, deposits included.

One low item is deliberately left open: if the withdrawals-root computation hits a provider error on every attempt, a block whose state root is also wrong is retried rather than rejected. That matches upstream's existing `parent_state()?` behaviour.

The deposit reviewer was not run: revm, op-revm and alloy-evm are unchanged, and the sweep found no execution, receipt or gas plumbing change that OP routes through.

## Proofs and prestates

The lockfile delta reaches crates that kona-client and the SP1 guest programs build:
- `alloy-trie` 0.9.8
- reth-core 0.8.2
- `hashbrown`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `arrayvec` and `bitflags`

So the SP1 guest ELFs and verification keys change, and the kona prestate is expected to change. Confirm with the reproducible prestate build before release.

## Migration notes (operator-facing)

**New flags, denied on op-reth:** `--snap.v2`, `--cpu-cores`, `--engine.prewarm-reuse` and `--debug.lazy-kzg-settings`. Each is rejected at startup with an explanation.

**Behaviour changes:**
- `eth_call` with no `gas` field is capped at `--rpc.gascap`, 50M by default (paradigmxyz/reth#27586).
- JS tracers get a 5s default timeout and a recursion limit of 128, and `prestateTracer` omits empty accounts (paradigmxyz/reth#27903, revm-inspectors 0.44).
- The WebSocket `Origin` allowlist is enforced when one is configured (paradigmxyz/reth#27952).
- `--txpool.minimum-priority-fee` also applies to legacy and EIP-2930 transactions, using the gas price (paradigmxyz/reth#27720).
- The metrics endpoint serves gzip, and returns 503 beyond 4 concurrent scrapes (paradigmxyz/reth#27766).
- `RETH_DB_SYNC_MODE` is read from the environment (paradigmxyz/reth#27938).
- CLI validation is stricter (paradigmxyz/reth#27980–#27982).
- Trie cursor metrics are renamed (paradigmxyz/reth#27771).
- `--engine.storage-worker-count` and `--engine.account-worker-count` now size per block.

**Changed default with no effect on op-reth:** `--gpo.ignoreprice` moves from 0 to 2 wei, but op-reth's tip suggestion doesn't read it.

## Verification

All of these ran on this head, pinned at `fc4e457`, unless noted:

- `cargo check --workspace --tests`: passes.
- `just lint`: passes, including the upstream-mirror check (83 mirrors, none stale).
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features`: 4699 passed, 17 skipped.
- Doctests: all pass.
- `just check-sp1-guest-lock` and `just check-sp1-guest-precompile-patches`: both pass.
- **CLI surface snapshot:** regenerated and reviewed. The new flags and default changes are listed above.
- **Fork:** CI on ethereum-optimism/reth#56 is 30/30 green at `fc4e457`, the pinned head.

topPRs.title: op-zk-proposer: adopt copies of our next game instead of walking past them
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #24356 (which is stacked on #24249); review those first. This PR's own change is the last commit.

A game's UUID does not include its creator, and the proposer's next create can be computed from public data (the next timestamp, `parentIndex || super root preimage`, and the root hashed from it). After #24249 the proposer ignored a copy of its next game and walked one second forward, so a third party could delay creation with one copy per attempt. A copy the attacker challenged itself cost it only gas.

The proposer now adopts the game it finds at the UUID of its create, whoever created it: the same UUID means the same parent, timestamp, and claim, so it is the game the proposer planned. An adopted copy counts as owned for head selection, defense, resolution, closing, and fast finality. A third party cannot make the proposer prove more games or longer spans than its own chain needs, and a challenger of a copy loses its bond to our proof again.

Effect on operators:
- Copies of the proposer's games no longer delay creation. Logs say "Adopting the existing game at our create's uuid" with `occupant=Copy`.
- With fast finality on, the proposer also proves adopted copies.
- Foreign ancestors of in-progress signer games, including ones chosen by versions before #24249, count as owned again and are defended. This removes the upgrade step in #24249's BREAKING CHANGE note.

Reasons the diff does not show:
- Restarts: the proposer keeps no state on disk. After a restart it re-adopts every foreign parent (above the anchor) of a game it owns, since only its own proposer chooses its games' parents. Without this, a restart would stop defending a copy that our games build on, and those games would lose their bonds when it lost. Before our first child exists, a restart replans the same timestamp and adopts the copy again at the collision.
- The UUID does not fix everything that lets a copy carry the chain, so a copy is not adopted when it lost, is challenged past its prove deadline, was created while ZK games were not respected (no child can be created on it), or binds an l1Head before the L1 block its root needs. The last one is a copy made from unsafe L2 data before the batch reaches L1: its claim is right but its proof can never bind that l1Head, so it loses when challenged, and our games built on it would lose their bonds. The check runs on every adoption path (collision, a create whose confirmation timed out, and the creation guard following its game after a reorg), against a fresh supernode query. Creation then walks one second forward as before.
- Adoption and the creation guard are published under one state lock, and the per-sync prune keeps the guard's game, so an adopted copy that the confirmed pin has not cached yet is not forgotten.
- Adopted copies stay unvalidated records, like other foreign games: a collision copy has the root the proposer computed and passes the l1Head check above, and a re-adopted one was chosen by our own proposer.
- No span check on re-adopted parents. Only parents chosen by versions before #24249 can exceed the span cap, and defending them is what those versions do.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/70

topPRs.title: op-challenger: add challenge-latest-zk-game subcommand
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body: Adds a `challenge-latest-zk-game` subcommand that challenges the newest unchallenged ZK game from the given creators, so a scheduled job can check that op-zk-proposer defends its valid games by proving them. It is a subcommand rather than a separate script so it runs from the shipped op-challenger image. The ZK `list-claims` report also gains `gameCreator`. Related to ethereum-optimism/proofs-team#22.
